s: "No State shall… pass any… Law impairing the Obligation of Contracts."
The Marshall Court applied the clause vigorously.
It protected land grants (Fletcher v. Peck, 1810) and corporate charters (Dartmouth College, 1819), though it applied only to contracts already in existence (Ogden v. Saunders, 1827).
Home Building & Loan v. Blaisdell (1934) upheld a Depression-era mortgage moratorium, and the clause has been modest since.
The clause limits only states and only retroactive impairment.
The federal government is constrained instead by due process.
